newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly down at 8.2990 against the U.S. dollar on Monday from last Friday's 8.2988 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market in quiet trading, dealers said.
The yuan opened up at 8.2985 but fell to an intra-day low of 8.30 early in the session and then rose to move between 8.2985 and 8.2990 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2978.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2985, traders said.
Dealers said the yuan's rising momentum slowed following a 16-month high set last Friday but strong pro-yuan sentiment continued.
"The yuan mainly consolidated around 8.2990, strengthening 8.30 as a support level," said one dealer.

"Slight falls in early trading apparantly had no impact on its long-term prospects," a second dealer said. "Today's intra-day high of 8.2978 is the highest over the past 16 months, which proves the yuan's rising trend."
Dealers expect the yuan to move up slightly on Tuesday.
The yuan closed marginally up at 7.4314 from 7.4550 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0731 from 1.0726 against the Hong Kong dollar.
